title: Acme first-line agent scope
summary: First-line agents at Acme can discuss options, explain notices, and signpost support routes. They cannot confirm payment arrangements, grant extensions, or waive charges without escalation.
body_markdown:
Acme City Council first-line agents are authorised to:

- explain the current notice or recovery stage
- signpost residents to support routes (CTR, debt advice)
- capture structured case notes
- route to the Revenues Specialist team
- log vulnerability-sensitive signals

First-line agents are NOT authorised to:
- confirm or negotiate payment arrangements
- grant extensions without specialist approval
- waive charges or costs
- make entitlement decisions

When in doubt, route to the Revenues Specialist team.
do_say_text: I can explain what this notice means and point you to the right support, but I'll need to get a specialist involved to confirm next steps.
do_not_say_text: Do not imply that you can confirm an arrangement or grant an extension.

title: Acme Revenues Specialist team — when to route
summary: Route to the Revenues Specialist team for: summons/liability order stage, complex arrears, vulnerability-sensitive cases requiring tailored handling, and cases where first-line scope is exceeded.
body_markdown:
The Revenues Specialist team handles:
- summons and liability order stage cases
- complex arrangement requests
- vulnerability-sensitive cases needing tailored review
- cases where breathing space may apply
- cases where the resident disputes the liability

To route:
- capture a clear case note with all relevant facts
- log the escalation reason
- inform the resident that a specialist will follow up
- set a callback marker if needed

SLA: Specialist team targets contact within 2 working days for standard referrals.
do_say_text: I'm going to refer this to our specialist team who are best placed to help with this. They will be in touch within [timeframe].
do_not_say_text: Do not confirm what the specialist will or will not do. Do not commit to an outcome.

title: Acme Council Tax Reduction signposting
summary: First-line agents should signpost eligible residents to the CTR application process. Do not make eligibility decisions. Direct to the online application or customer service team for assessment.
body_markdown:
When a resident may be eligible for Council Tax Reduction:

- inform the resident that CTR may reduce their bill
- do not confirm or imply eligibility
- direct to the CTR application: acmecitycouncil.gov.uk/ctr (synthetic placeholder)
- or offer to transfer to the Benefits team for an informal check

CTR can reduce the bill significantly for eligible residents and is worth signposting in all low-income or benefits cases.
do_say_text: Based on what you've told me, it might be worth checking whether you qualify for Council Tax Reduction, which could reduce your bill. I can point you to where to apply.
do_not_say_text: Do not say they will get CTR or that they qualify. This requires an assessment.

title: Acme vulnerability-sensitive call handling
summary: When a vulnerability signal is present, slow the call pace, use supportive language, avoid pressured questioning, and consider specialist routing. Record the signal in the case note.
body_markdown:
Acme City Council requires agents to handle calls involving vulnerability signals with care.

When a vulnerability signal is detected:
- slow the pace of the call
- simplify language and avoid jargon
- do not pressure the resident for information they are not comfortable sharing
- acknowledge what the resident has shared with empathy
- consider whether specialist routing is appropriate
- record the vulnerability signal in the case note (category, not personal detail)

Vulnerability is not always obvious. Always remain open to signals throughout the call.
do_say_text: Thank you for sharing that with me. I want to make sure we handle this in the right way for you.
do_not_say_text: Do not minimise or dismiss vulnerability disclosures. Do not ask for medical details.
